newsletter.subject: A cheaper sodium battery from Corvane
newsletter.text:
Researchers at the Corvane Institute say they have built a sodium-ion battery cell that keeps 90% of its capacity after 1,400 charge cycles.

The cell uses no cobalt or lithium, and the team estimates it would cost about 30% less to make than a comparable lithium-ion cell. The catch: it stores less energy for its weight, so the team is aiming at home storage and grid use rather than cars.

The work was published in the Journal of Applied Electrochemistry. A pilot line is planned for 2028.
